a: CSP restricts which scripts/resources can load, reducing XSS impact.
HSTS tells browsers to use HTTPS only for a site for a period of time.
SameSite cookie attribute limits cross-site sending of cookies (Lax/Strict/None).
HttpOnly cookies cannot be read by JavaScript, reducing XSS token theft.
Secure cookies are only sent over HTTPS.
Authorization Code flow redirects users to log in and returns a code the app exchanges for tokens.
PKCE protects public OAuth clients by binding the code exchange to a secret verifier.
A refresh token obtains new access tokens without re-login; store it carefully.
An access token authorizes API calls for a limited time.
Session fixation forces a user into an attacker-known session ID — rotate IDs on login.
Open redirects send users to untrusted URLs; validate redirect targets.
SSRF tricks a server into requesting internal resources on the attacker's behalf.
Path traversal uses ../ sequences to access files outside the intended directory.
Use HTTPS, CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, and careful CORS.
